scope: Callback-owner correction: matched Release CLI product builds, six synthetic fixtures, encode/decode, two interleaved rounds on this ARM64 Mac. No universal speed, isolated-host, device, pure-kernel or full-workspace claim.

policy.latencyStatistic: ratio of candidate/baseline medians within each round
policy.memoryStatistic: ratio of maximum observed per-process peak RSS within each round; median and p95 also reported
policy.trigger: A reproducible median-latency or peak-memory increase over 5%; observed crossings require investigation, not automatic waiver.

method.outputEqualityScope: Baseline/candidate bytes were compared before timing each operation in each round. Timed outputs went to /dev/null and were not compared individually.
method.statistics: Percent change = 100 * (candidate / baseline - 1). Median is the middle-pair mean; nearest-rank p95 uses sorted sample 19 of 20. Spread is minimum/maximum and median absolute deviation. Paired diagnostics align the two binaries at each loop iteration. No inferential confidence interval or significance claim is made.
method.order: Five warmups then twenty samples; adjacent baseline/candidate runs alternate first position each iteration, reversed across the second round.
method.verification: All 96 recorded latency/RSS distributions and 48 throughput values independently recalculated; executed runner, build/provenance/helper, binaries and 46 current shipping source hashes matched.

environment.power: AC power, 100% charged at both snapshots
environment.thermal: pmset reported no recorded thermal/performance warning at both endpoints; no continuous thermal trace was captured.
environment.competingCodecWork: Before/after snapshots contain no competing codec benchmark, fuzz target or compiler/build job. Those jobs had completed, per coordinator. Snapshots are not continuous process monitoring.
environment.interpretation: This was a local matched paired comparison with ordinary desktop activity, not an exclusive or fully idle host. The VM process CPU snapshot fell during the short run; this is a documented possible source of nonstationary noise.

disposition.reason: All 24 median-latency and maximum-peak-RSS comparisons remain below +5% in both alternating-order rounds. The nearest-rank p95 crossings are isolated to one round for each affected case. The finite paired comparison is sufficient to screen this narrow callback-owner correction for a reproducible PERF-03 regression under the recorded environment. It does not prove the tiny differences are real or eliminate effects of desktop contention.
disposition.tailLimit: Five one-round p95 increases exceed 5%; flat-19 decode round 1 has a +114.054% maximum-latency outlier. Maximum latency for lossless16-512 decode rises in both rounds; median and p95 do not reproduce a threshold crossing. No tail-latency improvement or guarantee is claimed.
disposition.repeatCondition: Request a fresh isolated-host run before stronger kernel/tail-latency or tiny-speedup claims, or if a subsequent controlled comparison produces a repeatable >5% median-latency/peak-memory increase. Do not silently combine the excluded loaded run with these samples.
disposition.memoryLimit: Darwin time -l reports per-process lifetime maximum RSS. This is not algorithm workspace, peak pixel allocation, callback allocation count or a physical-device ceiling. Existing direct allocation/copy evidence is separate.
disposition.fidelityAndSize: All 24 baseline/candidate output checks are exact. Encoded size is therefore unchanged, including lossless output; no >1% lossless-size trigger exists. Independent oracle tolerances and earlier djpeg benchmark exclusions are unchanged.
